 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0008
 Lindsey Smith, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
March 11, 2024
Plaintiff's counsel:
Andrew Lewis, Johnson & Lowery Injury Lawyers
PARTIES
Plaintiff Lindsey Smith is an individual residing in Texas who was the driver of a vehicle involved in the collision described
below. Defendant is an automobile insurance company authorized to write policies in the State of Texas, which issued the policy
under which Plaintiff seeks benefits and against which Plaintiff brings this action.
FACTS
On April 10, 2023, Plaintiff was lawfully parked in a commercial parking lot in Baytown when another vehicle, insured by
Defendant's policyholder, backed out of an adjacent space and struck the driver's side of Plaintiff's vehicle. The impact was
sudden and forceful. Plaintiff reported the collision promptly and submitted a claim to Defendant under the applicable coverage.
Defendant has acknowledged coverage in part but has not paid the full amount owed for Plaintiff's losses.
NEGLIGENCE
The policyholder's driver failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to yield to vehicles and pedestrians in the lot, and backed the
vehicle without ensuring the way was clear. These acts constitute negligence. Defendant is responsible under the terms of its
policy and applicable Texas law for the covered losses caused by its insured's negligence, and it further owed Plaintiff a duty to
handle the claim in good faith and to pay benefits owed within the time required by the Texas Insurance Code.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff sustained a whiplash injury to the neck and upper back, with ongoing pain, stiffness,
headaches, and reduced range of motion. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses for examination, imaging, and physical therapy,
has missed time from work, and has experienced pain and mental anguish. Plaintiff seeks recovery of economic and
non-economic damages within the limits of the policy and as allowed by law, in an amount of $180,000.00, together with
statutory interest, court costs, and attorney's fees as permitted under Texas law.
